logs.notes: [Crop Status] Potato harvest weight: 2 lbs 14 oz.

[Crop Status] Big harvest day! Harvested many tomatoes and green beans (both actively producing). Harvested 3 potato plants (2 volunteer, 1 intentional) yielding 2 lbs 13 oz total of large tubers. Heights logged: Carrots (24"), 1st Sow Beans (26"), 2nd Sow Beans (18"), Tomatoes (52"), Potatoes (16"), Corn (104").
[Crop Status] First amazing sweet corn harvested! Corn height reached 108". Tomatoes rebounded to 57", and 2nd Sow Bush Beans reached 17".
[Crop Status] Sweet Corn surged past 100" reaching 103". Carrots (22") and 1st Sow Bush Beans (25") showing continued vertical progress.
[Corn Milestones] Corn started silking on Monday, July 27, supported by deep-soaking irrigation interventions.

[Crop Status] Major heat-driven growth explosion logged across corn (67"), cucumbers (64"), and tomatoes (50"). Potatoes showing flowers and potato berries, signaling transition to active underground tuber-bulking phase. First cucumbers harvested.

[Crop Status] Audibled from fish fertilizer drench to dry pellet side-dressing due to restrictive mature crop canopy density. Completed targeted Coop Poop distributions across corn, tomatoes, and carrots.
[Precipitation] Massive storm delivered 2.1" of rainfall on July 8. Irrigation manually shut off to avoid waterlogging the sub-surface soil.
[Crop Status] Peas Cleared: Spring pea vines removed. Soil preparing for late-summer planting strategy.
[Soaker Hose System] Transitioned out of full standby into a defensive watering interval of once every 2 days (1-hour deep soak) to counter local cucumber root saturation.
[Beneficial Nematodes] 2 million units deployed via Chapin G362D sprayer at dusk across 16 corn clusters and cucumber footprint.
[Pest Defense] Baby rabbits breached perimeter; physical fence gap reinforcement updated.
[Pest Warning] Spotted yellow and green cucumber beetles. Bacterial wilt & leaf mottling observed.
Noticed corn dropped from 108" to 104", because of weight of corn.
7 carrots have gone to seed. Will see if the underlying carrots are still good.
BIG HARVEST DAY! 6 ears of corn, 0.8 lbs green beans, many tomatoes, corn is looking great.
Potatoes are dying, look reasonably ready to harvest.
logs.author: Wyatt

logs.notes: The corn has produced10! cobs Yes ten cobs! on the other hand the midnights are producing less than the early girl?! The Green beans are also producing slowly?! Now ten carrots have gone seed it makes me worried/paranoid not knowing what will happen.
logs.author: Wyatt

logs.notes: DAD and I pulled up the carrots that have gone to seed! We got 8 carrots and somehow 1PARSNIP?! We will try them anyway! They will probably be VERY BITTER!
logs.author: Wyatt

logs.notes: This was too late to pick the corn!  It's all starchy and not sweet.  Next year we need to pick when the silks are still fresh!
BIG HARVEST DAY! DAD and I picked 218 tomatoes, 5 ears of corn, 1.3 lbs. of carrots, and last but not least 1.1 lbs. of green beans!
logs.author: Wyatt

logs.notes: Great harvest day. The green beans are still heavily producing. The plants have reached their maximum height. This weekend dad and I are going to pick carrots!
logs.author: Wyatt

logs.notes: Huge harvest of carrots. Now in soil-filled buckets in garage.
